Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: IBM ending visa sponsorship for most roles in IBM Consulting: What will happen to employees?
Article Text:
IBM says it will halt several visa and Green Card sponsorships.

'Funny how corporate calculus changes'

What will happen to affected employees?

Will all H-1B visa holders of IBM be laid off?

1. Employees currently on H-1B visas

2. Employees whose Green Card applications are in progress

There are different stages in the employment-based Green Card process. If PERM is not filed, the employee may have to find another employer to start the process from scratch.

If the PERM application is pending, a new employer generally has to begin its own PERM process.

If PERM is approved but I-140 is not filed, then the employee will generally need a new employer to file a fresh Green Card petition.

If the I-140 is pending, then the employee may also need a new employer to restart the process. There are limited protections if an associated I-485 has already been pending for 180 days.

If the I-140 is approved, then the employee may retain the original priority date, even if IBM withdraws the petition, subject to USCIS rules.

If the I-485 is pending for 180 days or more, the employee may qualify to transfer the Green Card application to another employer, provided the new job is in the same or a similar occupational classification.

Tech giant IBM has announced that it is ending certain Green Card sponsorship and H-1B visa programs within its consulting business. The company said that the decision has been prompted by skill availability in the US, meaning the company does not need to bring in foreign skilled workers. This does not apply to the entire company but only to IBM Consulting, which employs 150,000 people globally.IBM Consulting is the services and technology-advisory arm of IBM (International Business Machines). It helps other companies modernise their businesses, adopt new technologies and manage large-scale IT operations. It basically covers IT consulting, AI, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and business transformation etc. The workforce comprises software engineers and developers, IT consultants, data scientists and AI specialists, cloud architects, cybersecurity professionals, project managers and business analysts.Inspector General of the US Department of Labor, Anthony D'Esposito, reacted to the announcement and called it funny. He said the announcement was obviously a reaction to the Trump administration's crackdown on visa and Green Card abuse. "@IBMis pulling back on visa sponsorships. Funny how the corporate calculus changes when scrutiny shows up...Ifyour business model depends on nobody checking, find a new business model," he said.Bloomberg reported that the affected employees will have the option to leave the US and continue working for IBM outside the US or leave the company at the end of the year.Many aspects of IBM's announcement remain unclear: like whether the announcement is for new sponsorships of Green Cards or whether those who are in the Green Card queue will be affected.If they want to remain in the US, they will have to find a new employer as IBM is likely to stop their visa sponsorship.
Article Summary: IBM Consulting is the services and technology-advisory arm of IBM (International Business Machines) It helps other companies modernise their businesses, adopt new technologies and manage large-scale IT operations. The workforce comprises software engineers and developers, IT consultants, data scientists and AI specialists.

Article Title: 'No flights will shift from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai airport': Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis
Article Text:
“I have written to them to first develop Terminal 1B, shift 1A to 1B and then take down the existing 1A terminal,” Fadnavis said.





MUMBAI: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has opposed Mumbai airport operator’s plan to shift international flights to 14 destinations to Navi Mumbai airport from next summer, saying no flights would be moved out of Mumbai.He has written to the union civil aviation minister on the issue.Fadnavis on Tuesday said he has proposed an alternative sequence for Terminal 1 (T1) redevelopment that would allow the existing terminal to remain operational until its replacement is ready.“I have written to them to first develop Terminal 1B, shift 1A to 1B and then take down the existing 1A terminal,” Fadnavis said.His proposal would allow the airport to demolish and reconstruct T1 in stages rather than shut it down entirely before starting construction of the replacement.The Airports Authority of India (AAI), a central government entity, holds 26% stake in Mumbai airport, with the remaining 74% held by Adani Airport Holdings Ltd (AAHL).The issue of moving some flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai airport has been contentious.Last month, Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) informed airlines about its plans to reduce international operations at Terminal 2 (T2) by a third from the Summer 2027 schedule, beginning March-end, to accommodate 5 million passengers per annum (mppa) of domestic traffic displaced by the first phase of T1 demolition.Last week, AAHL informed the ministry that it plans to move flights connecting Mumbai with 14 international destinations to Navi Mumbai from next summer.The destinations are Bahrain, Dammam, Dhaka, Doha, Fujairah, Jakarta, Jeddah, Kathmandu, Kuwait City, Madinah, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Riyadh and Sharjah.MIAL has told airlines that it cannot accommodate their requested Summer 2027 slots and that a temporary transition out of T2 will be necessary.The proposed shift has faced resistance from airlines. The International Air Transport Association (IATA), which represents airlines globally, had urged the ministry to adopt a phased redevelopment approach, whereby portions of T1 would be demolished and reconstructed sequentially to avoid a wholesale loss of capacity.The entire 15-mppa (million passengers per annum) T1 is scheduled to be demolished by March 2028, with reconstruction beginning only thereafter.The new T1 is expected to be ready by December 2030. Airlines sources said that shutting T1 completely would leave Mumbai airport with a substantial capacity deficit for three years or more."The operational complexity at T1 stems from its fragmented infrastructure, with T1A, T1B and T1C not functioning as independent, full-scale terminals," said a source."While T1A remains unusable due to infrastructure constraints and obsolete equipment, T1C has only six contact gates and depends on T1B for passenger check-in. Passenger processing is consequently split across T1B's two security hold areas and T1C, restricting passenger movement and affecting asset utilisation and service quality," the source added.The operational interdependence between T1 and T2 also extends to the airside. MIAL has proposed a 3.042-km underground airside tunnel connecting the T1 and T2 aprons, as well as additional aircraft parking stands proposed south of runway 09-27.Currently, when T2 runs short of parking stands, some aircraft are parked at the T1 apron, requiring passengers and baggage to be transported between the two via a perimeter road and runway 14-32.The airport operator cited lengthy transfer times and monsoon-related delays as reasons for the proposed tunnel.
Article Summary: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has opposed Mumbai airport operator’s plan to shift international flights to 14 destinations to Navi Mumbai airport from next summer. He has written to the union civil aviation minister on the issue. “I have written to them to first develop Terminal 1B, shift 1A to 1B and then take down the existing 1A terminal,” he said.

Article Title: India, Oman begin naval exercise as Arabian Sea security takes centre stage
Article Text:
INS Surat at the Port of Muscat in Oman for a bilateral exercise. (Image credit: Indian Navy)

Why these waters matter

Working with partners in the region

A large share of India's crude oil imports and exports passes through the Arabian Sea and the western Indian Ocean. Any disruption in these waters can quickly affect freight rates, insurance costs and supply chains.Against this backdrop, Indian Naval Ship (INS) Surat arrived in Muscat, Oman, on November 8 to participate in the 15th edition of the bilateral maritime exercise Naseem Al Bahr, followed by a Coordinated Patrol (CORPAT) with the Royal Navy of Oman.The exercise includes harbour and sea phases, with cross-deck visits, operational interactions and sporting events. The aim is to allow personnel from both navies to exchange operational experience and best practices, improve interoperability and strengthen mutual understanding.The port call is in line with the government's MAHASAGAR vision, short for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions. It also builds on the 13th meeting of the India-Oman Joint Military Cooperation Committee, held on November 24, 2025.Press Information Bureau+1The western maritime approaches connect India's ports with the Gulf, the Red Sea, Europe and the east coast of Africa. The Gulf of Aden and the waters off Somalia are particularly important because they provide access to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal, a major shipping route between Asia and Europe.Any disruption caused by conflict, piracy or attacks on merchant vessels can affect India's energy security and export industries.The Indian Navy has maintained an anti-piracy deployment in the Gulf of Aden since 2008. In July 2026, INS Trikand responded to an attempted pirate attack on the merchant vessel MV Golden Arsenal, approximately 300 nautical miles (550 km) east-northeast of Djibouti. The warship deployed a boarding team, supported by a P-8I maritime patrol aircraft, to secure the vessel and assess the situation.In 2026, the Navy also launched Operation Urja Suraksha to protect merchant shipping and India's energy interests amid the worsening security situation in West Asia.Its role extends beyond anti-piracy patrols. INS Tarkash, deployed in the western Indian Ocean from January 2025, supported Combined Task Force 150 of the 47-nation Combined Maritime Forces (CMF). On March 31, 2025, the warship intercepted a vessel carrying more than 2,500 kg of narcotics.On October 14, 2026, the Indian Navy relinquished command of Combined Task Force 154, the CMF's maritime training task force, at a ceremony in Bahrain. During its eight-month command, the Navy oversaw multinational training and capacity-building initiatives involving personnel from 39 countries.INS Trikand visited Maputo, Mozambique, in March 2026, where it conducted joint training with the Mozambique Navy. On departure, the warship also undertook joint surveillance of Mozambique's exclusive economic zone, with Mozambican naval personnel on board.INS Sunayna's deployments under the IOS SAGAR initiative in 2025 and 2026 further demonstrated India's efforts to strengthen regional maritime cooperation. The 2025 mission included 44 naval personnel from nine partner countries, while the 2026 deployment brought together 38 personnel from 16 partner nations for multinational training and operational engagements across the Indian Ocean region.The Navy's operational reach was on display again on November 2, when INS Kolkata, supported by Indian Air Force assets, helped rescue all 20 crew members of the Iranian fishing vessel Azini, which had been hijacked by armed pirates off Somalia.The operation, conducted over 48 hours more than 3,000 km from Mumbai, involved maritime surveillance, marine commandos and an IAF C-17 aircraft that airdropped additional personnel. The crew was rescued without casualties.
Article Summary: A large share of India's crude oil imports and exports passes through the Arabian Sea and the western Indian Ocean. Any disruption in these waters can quickly affect freight rates, insurance costs and supply chains. The Indian Navy has maintained an anti-piracy deployment in the Gulf of Aden since 2008.

Article Title: Nvidia shares plunge 8% amid investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese spy'
Article Text:
Nvidia has grown into one of the world's most valuable businesses and a key supplier to major technology companies

What it means for the stock

Nvidia shares plunged over 8% in opening trade on Monday after an internal investigation was announced into whether chief executive Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation triggered concerns about his future at the AI chipmaker. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company.Earlier today, Nvidia shares dropped 5% in premarket trading. Huang is facing a board-level investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The inquiry follows a media report linking him to a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing.Last month, The New York Times reported that Huang had been in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who is not related to him. US authorities investigated her and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.According to Bernstein, the controversy is unlikely to dent demand for Nvidia's products.The allegations could become a "heavy distraction" for the company or, in a worst-case scenario, provide "significant ammunition" to lawmakers from both political parties, brokerage Bernstein said on Monday.However, the firm warned that regulatory risks could increase as the expansion of AI infrastructure becomes a more prominent political issue.The latest developments are also likely to keep Nvidia at the centre of the debate.Bernstein maintains an "outperform" rating on Nvidia, with a price target of $400.Nadia El Bilassy, senior market analyst at Equiti Group told Reuters, “This was just the cherry on top for investors looking to pull out of AI-linked stocks. It's a very bad headline that's affecting tech stocks.”The attention on Nvidia could ease later this week "when we have more important things to discuss, like the inflation data," she added.Nvidia's technology has featured prominently in several major developments in the tech industry, from video gaming and self-driving vehicles to cloud computing and artificial intelligence.The company made early investments in AI under Huang's leadership. When ChatGPT was launched in late 2022, Nvidia's chips were already well placed to benefit from the sharp increase in demand for computing power to support AI.Nvidia has since grown into one of the world's most valuable businesses and a key supplier to major technology companies. Its valuation surged from $420 billion in late 2022 to $4.5 trillion as of November 6.Separately, US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing company that buys Nvidia products, over suspicions that it helped Beijing obtain advanced AI chips from Nvidia despite restrictions prohibiting their shipment to China.The New York Times reported last month that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, had developed a close relationship with the Nvidia chief and allegedly passed information directly to Beijing.Nvidia said an independent committee of its directors would supervise the investigation, with assistance from external independent legal counsel.The company also said Huang fully supports the review and has pledged to cooperate with the investigation.
Article Summary: N Nvidia shares plunged over 8% in opening trade on Monday after an internal investigation was announced into whether chief executive Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The inquiry follows a media report linking him to a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company.

Article Title: Rs 3-crore Defender, horse race with SUV prize, 150 dishes: Anant Singh goes all out for daughter's wedding
Article Text:
Mokama MLA Anant Singh is ensuring his daughter’s big day will be difficult to miss.





PATNA: A Rs 3-crore Land Rover Defender for the bridegroom, a BMW worth around Rs 1 crore for the younger son, a wedding venue spread over more than 10 bighas, a horse race with an SUV as the top prize and a menu boasting over 150 dishes.If weddings are about making a statement, Mokama MLA Anant Singh is ensuring his daughter’s big day will be difficult to miss. Add Bollywood and Bhojpuri artists, six models from Dubai and invitations for some of the country’s biggest political names, and the celebrations in Ladma village have become an event with all eyes on it.Known for his flamboyant lifestyle and larger-than-life public persona, Singh is preparing for the Nov 25 wedding of his younger daughter, Shivangi Singh , to Rishikesh Kumar alias Ankit, son of commandant Ranvijay Kumar of Krishnanagar in Bihta, Patna. Rishikesh holds an MBA degree and has lived in the United States for around 11 years.The luxury Defender, estimated to cost between Rs 2.5 crore and Rs 3 crore, has already reached Ladma. The BMW, worth around Rs 1 crore, is for Singh’s youngest son Abhinav, whose ‘janeu’ ceremony will be held alongside the wedding. The vehicles have become a talking point in the village even before the wedding festivities have gathered full pace.The wedding venue is being developed across more than 10 bighas, while a separate ground spread over nearly 12 bighas is being prepared for the horse-racing competition. The scale of the arrangements has prompted Singh to plan for around four lakh visitors, with preparations allowing for the possibility of even more guests.The wedding decorations are being planned on a similarly imposing scale. A nearly 30-foot-high stage, inspired by Jaipur’s Patrakar Chauraha, is being built for the ‘jaimala’ ceremony. Flowers are being sourced from China and Bengaluru, decorative materials from different parts of the country, and tent workers have been brought in from Mau in Uttar Pradesh. A specialised event company has been entrusted with the work.Puneet Kumar, Singh’s eldest son-in-law, said the Defender was chosen by Shivangi and gifted to her on her birthday. She completed her schooling in Delhi and post-graduation from Delhi University.The family has a history of elaborate wedding arrangements. “I was married to Raj Nandini, eldest daughter of Singh, in 2015. In my wedding, only parking was made on around 4 bighas of land,” said the son-in-law.The horse race, scheduled for Nov 25 from 2pm to 4pm, is expected to draw riders from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana and other states. Manish Kumar, an associate of Singh, said the winner would receive an SUV, the runner-up a motorcycle and the third-place finisher a scooter.Food, too, is being treated as an event in itself. The menu will feature more than 150 varieties, ranging from traditional Bihari preparations to dishes from other states. Sweets will include kaju katli and Silao khaja, the Nalanda speciality known for its distinctive 52-layer structure.Singh has also expressed his wish to invite PM Narendra Modi , former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, RJD president Lalu Prasad and Tejashwi Prasad Yadav. Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar has already received an invitation.Singh, who has been asked by the Supreme Court to surrender on Dec 4 in Dularchand murder case, has said there will be no political distinction among guests and visitors from anywhere in the world, including India and Pakistan, will be welcome.
Article Summary: Mokama MLA Anant Singh is preparing for the Nov 25 wedding of his younger daughter, Shivangi Singh, to Rishikesh Kumar alias Ankit. The luxury Defender, estimated to cost between Rs 2.5 crore and Rs 3 crore, has already reached Ladma. The BMW, worth around Rs 1 crore, is for Singh’s youngest son Abhinav.

Article Title: Marriage and motherhood should not affect career: Karnataka high court
Article Text:
In an order passed on Oct 29, Justice Lalitha Kanneganti disposed of a petition filed by the woman's husband, who resides in Mumbai (AI Image)

​'Motherhood doesn't confine a woman to single place'​

'

Motherhood doesn

't confine a woman to single place'





BENGALURU: Marriage, motherhood and raising children should not affect a woman's professional career or tie her down to one place, Karnataka high court has observed in a recent judgement, clearing an ophthalmologist's relocation to the United Kingdom.In an order passed on Oct 29, Justice Lalitha Kanneganti disposed of a petition filed by the woman's husband, who resides in Mumbai. He had challenged the order of a Bengaluru family court that directed him to deliver the original passport of their minor child to his wife and provide consent to obtain a visa to travel to the United Kingdom.He had challenged another order rejecting his request for a change in interim custody of the minor child from the wife's family to his family, along with other consequential relief.The wife argued she had been taking care of the child since 2019 when they were thrown out of their residence in Mumbai. According to her, employment in the UK provides a better and more secure financial position, enabling her to provide the child with stable housing, education, healthcare and extracurricular opportunities."Marriage and motherhood do not require her to remain confined to a particular place," the judge said, specifying conditions for mutual visits: The mother shall allow regular audio and video calls between the father and the child at least for 20 minutes a day; the father shall get parenting time with the child during school holidays; twice in a year during the child's holidays, the mother shall send the boy to India to spend 75% of the vacation with the father; the father could go to the United Kingdom to meet the child for 75% of the holidays.

The wife argued she had been taking care of the child since 2019.

Article Title: Crackers versus vehicles: What really contributes to Delhi's Diwali pollution?
Article Text:
Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8

Diwali fireworks add to existing pollution

Vehicles: An endless source

Diwali fireworks release fine particles that rapidly worsen air quality

Crackers push particulate levels sharply higher

Low wind speeds and temperature inversion make it harder to disperse pollutants

What crackers bring to the table

Delhi's PM2

Weather is the difference

Can't ignore either one





Every year, Delhi’s Diwali pollution debate is between two sources: firecrackers and vehicles. But the latest pollution data suggests the problem is more complex. Pollution can spike sharply in the case of fireworks, but vehicles are one of the biggest contributors to the city’s everyday PM2.5 burden.The real worry is what will happen when these emissions combine with an atmosphere that is already polluted and with bad weather.The Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) has set up a new Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory (AATAL), which gives a useful picture of Delhi’s pollution mix.Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5 %), road dust (10.9 %) and waste burning (5 %).Even around Diwali the transport contribution was still substantial. Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8, the largest identified source, estimated the IITM’s Decision Support System (DSS).The figure explains why vehicular pollution cannot be seen as a seasonal problem: unlike fireworks, traffic emissions persist throughout the year.But firecrackers cause pollution of a different kind of episode. They tend to emit their emissions over a relatively short period of time, and they emit fine particles and gasses that can quickly degrade air quality.The effect was visible on the night of Diwali. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee’s data reported on November 9 showed that at Akshardham the PM2.5 concentration was at 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11pm. This was an hourly reading, not a 24 hour average, but gives an idea of how intense the spike of pollution was.Delhi’s AQI had already fallen to 382 on November 6, its worst pre-Diwali reading in eight years, according to CPCB data. It averaged 376 on Diwali November 8, from 369 a day earlier. AQI stood at 368 at 7am on November 9. Of the 54 monitoring stations that reported valid readings, 50 were above 300 and 15 entered the severe category.At the time when fireworks are set off, the Delhi atmosphere is becoming less conducive to dispersing pollutants. The Air Quality Early Warning System said dispersion is difficult when ventilation index is less than 6,000 square meters per second and average wind speeds are below 10kmph. Low temperatures and temperature inversion can also trap pollutants near the ground.That means fireworks smoke doesn’t just disappear when the party’s over. It adds to the existing emissions from vehicles, industry, dust and regional sources, thus adding to the particulate load.The latest figures do not allow for simply blaming either crackers or vehicles. Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily. Cracker restrictions can curb the festive spike, but sustained improvement will depend on curbing transport emissions, controlling road dust and industrial pollution, and improving regional coordination. One night of action cannot fix a year-long problem of air pollution in Delhi.
Article Summary: Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5%) and road dust (10.9%) Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily.

Article Title: Samsung set to become South Korea's first company with 200 trillion won in cash
Article Text:
Samsung's cash reserves to cross 200 trillion won as AI chip demand grows

Samsung Electronics is on course to become the first company in South Korea to build cash assets of more than 200 trillion won ($146.6 billion), with the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor boom strengthening its financial position.The chipmaker's cash reserves have nearly doubled over the past year, while its overall assets have also grown. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. This marks a rise of 24.8 trillion won from the 190 trillion won recorded at the end of the previous quarter, as reported by Yonhap news agency.The latest estimate is also almost twice the 108.5 trillion won the company held at the end of the third quarter of 2025.Samsung's total assets stood at 791.8 trillion won at the end of September, an increase of 32.4 trillion won over the preceding three months.The company's growing cash position is expected to be enough to cover the highest possible payout under its landmark shareholder return policy announced in August, market watchers estimate.Samsung had indicated that it would make between 90 trillion won and 110 trillion won available for shareholder returns in 2026.The company is also expected to announce its shareholder policy for the coming year at a board meeting scheduled for January.Alongside shareholder payouts, Samsung is preparing for a significant increase in spending on its semiconductor business.Investments in chipmaking infrastructure and research and development are expected to exceed 100 trillion won this year, marking a historic high. Of this amount, 84.4 trillion won is expected to go towards expanding its memory production facilities.Samsung expects the semiconductor supercycle to extend through next year, supported by continued investments in artificial intelligence and a crunch in memory supply.
Article Summary: Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Amit Pabari, managing director of CR Forex Advisors, said improving diplomatic expectations were already having an impact on energy prices."The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. On the upside, 94.40–94.50 is likely to act as the immediate resistance zone," Pabari said.Meanwhile, domestic equity markets opened lower on Monday. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. Article Title: Research claims that many companies in the US are calling back employees they fired and replaced by AI; and it is costing them more, as sacked employees now …
Article Text:
Areas where companies are finding AI falls short

Klarna and Ford adjust course

AI layoffs continue to climb

Nearly one in five US workers say they have experienced a surprising workplace reversal: their employer replaced them with artificial intelligence (AI), only to ask them to come back later, a report has found. According to new research from talent assessment firm SHL, this growing trend – which the firm calls “AI rebounding” – suggests several companies are learning the hard way that AI cannot do everything human employees can. And bringing those workers back is proving expensive.The SHL survey, conducted in June and July, and published recently, found that 19.1% of US respondents had been replaced by AI and subsequently asked to return to their jobs. Across both the US and the UK, that figure stood at 16%. However, those returning workers are not coming back on the old terms.According to SHL:51% demanded a substantial pay increase before agreeing to return.42% required written guarantees about their future job security.40% wanted clear transparency on how AI would be used in their roles.“Organisations are making fast, sometimes myopic, decisions about their people based on an incomplete picture of what their employees can do with or without AI.AI rebounding is what happens when a company automates a role before it has genuinely assessed the human capability inside it. The AI doesn’t deliver, the gap becomes obvious, and the business ends up rehiring the same experts they just let go of, at a far greater cost,” said Lucy Beaumont, global senior vice president of product and design at SHL, in a press release.SHL’s findings line up with a separate July survey from Robert Half. That study found that 32% of US hiring managers whose companies cut jobs because of AI eventually had to bring back the same or similar positions. Among those hiring managers, the gaps left by automation were clear:40% said the roles required institutional knowledge or context that AI could not replicate.39% cited relationship management.39% pointed to increased business demand.38% said the jobs needed more human oversight and quality control than the company expected.Several major companies have already run into these limits firsthand. For example, Swedish buy-now, pay-later firm Klarna recently began hiring human customer service representatives again after leaning heavily on AI chatbots.CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski acknowledged the company had gone too far with automation, Bloomberg reported. A Klarna spokesperson told Fortune that human agents were necessary “for complex, sensitive cases,” noting the company was directly hiring a “small number” of high-skilled workers to see where the “human touch” adds the most value.Similarly, automaker Ford made a move in June, hiring and promoting 350 experienced engineers after AI-powered quality control tools fell short of expectations. While Ford noted that AI has helped improve quality, a company representative told Fortune that “these engineers carry the hard-earned wisdom of decades of design,” adding that pairing AI with deep technical expertise is what actually gets results.Even as some employers backtrack, overall AI-driven job cuts are still rising sharply.As per the data from outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas, employers cited AI in 121,401 announced job cuts through October. That is already more than double the 54,836 AI-related layoffs announced during all of 2025. The report also said younger workers are taking the brunt of the shift. A study from the Stanford Digital Economy Lab found that employment among workers aged 22 to 25 in jobs heavily exposed to AI was 19% lower than it would have been if it had grown at the same pace as less-exposed fields.
Article Summary: 19.1% of US respondents had been replaced by AI and subsequently asked to return to their jobs. Across both the US and the UK, that figure stood at 16%. However, those returning workers are not coming back on the old terms.
